name: Kok-Kyya Valley
near: There are no permanent villages: at the head of the valley is a seasonal camp of ~20 yurts (the end of the road) and summer camps of yak herders. The last sizable settlement is At-Bashy; the town of Naryn is about 100 km as the crow flies (Nomad's Land) and 150–200 km by road. The earlier “Karaul-Tobe ~45 km” is a straight line across the ridges and is no guide for a trip.
elev: About 3300 m (canyon, Nomad's Land); the yurt camps at the head of the valley are on the order of 3300–3400 m (not precisely confirmed). TripAdvisor gives 3514 m — this is probably the elevation of Lake Kel-Suu.
short: Kok-Kyya is a remote border valley in the Ak-Sai basin with a winding canyon of the river of the same name (walls 300–400 m) and yurt camps — the base for the hike to Lake Kel-Suu.
desc: The Kok-Kyya River flows out of Lake Kel-Suu (Kol-Too and Sary-Beles mountains), meanders for about 40 km across the Kapshygay plateau, cutting a series of rock canyons, and joins the Kakshaal, which flows into China (Nomad's Land). The canyon walls rise 300–400 m, the granite gradually gives way to limestone, and dark cave entrances are visible in the rocks (eurasia.travel). The main occupation of the locals is yak breeding. The road ends at the head of the valley: here stand seasonal yurt camps (~20 yurts), from which it is 8–12 km to Kel-Suu on foot or on horseback, with a river ford. The valley lies in the border zone — a permit is needed, which is checked at the post after Kyndy Pass. In 2026 locals complained of trash and overloading by tourist traffic (time.kg, 14.08.2026).
guide: People often drive straight through Kok-Kyya on the way to Kel-Suu, and they shouldn't: stop at the canyon, where the river cuts through the plateau with walls of 300–400 meters, and look for the black cave entrances. Yak herders live here — you'll see herds of yaks on the meadows, and at the camp they'll pour you tea with kaymak. Stay overnight in a yurt at the head of the valley so you can set out for the lake at dawn, while the water at the ford is low. If you have time left, walk down the river — the change from granite to limestone is clearly visible in the walls. There is no signal here, so warn your family in advance.
see: The Kok-Kyya River canyon with walls of 300–400 m and caves; the change from granite to limestone; herds of yaks and summer camps; fords across the river; yurt camps at the head of the valley; the 8–12 km foot/horse route to Lake Kel-Suu.
skip: You aren't going to Kel-Suu — it's not worth spending 3 days and arranging a permit just for the valley. You count on comfort: the camps have mattresses on the floor, a stove and outdoor toilets. Late June is still cold and snowy, and from September the camps close.
diff: The road — high (4×4, gravel “washboard,” bogs, fords); staying at the camp — easy; the walk to the lake — moderate (~12 km round trip with almost no ascent, a ford — OunTravela). Elevation ~3300 m.
when: Mid-July to late August (NomadCar); the camps operate from late June to early September (kgnomad, 2026). TripAdvisor: season July to early September. In June snow is possible, in September there are night frosts, and in winter (down to −40 °C in neighboring Ak-Sai) the road is impassable.
hours: An open natural area in the border zone — permit only; the yurt camps are seasonal (late June to early September), and 2GIS gives “around the clock” for Kel-Suu Yurt Camp in season.
daytime: Morning — for the fords and the walk to the lake (the water rises by 30–50 cm after noon — NomadCar); evening — for the light in the canyon and on the slopes (editorial).
how: Bishkek → Naryn (≈350 km) → At-Bashy → Kyndy Pass (3400 m) and the border post → Ak-Sai valley → down the Kok-Kyya valley to the camps (the end of the road). From Naryn 150–200 km, 4–8 h (Kabar, OunTravela, kgnomad); 4×4 / SUV only.
needcar: Yes, a prepared 4×4 with an experienced local driver (clearance of 200–220 mm or more, low-range gear — NomadCar); there is no public transport.
self: With restrictions: the permit is arranged in advance (CBT Naryn — €30–50, tour.too.kg — 3000 som), and you can go only with a prepared 4×4 and a local driver; navigation and fords are dangerous without experience.
roadtype: Gravel/dirt with “washboard” from Naryn via Kyndy and Ak-Sai, then boggy sections and river fords (NomadCar); in the valley, a rutted dirt road to the camps; the At-Bashy — Kyndy — Torugart road was graded in 08.2026 (time.kg).
traveltime: Bishkek — Naryn ~5–6 h; Naryn — Kok-Kyya camps 4–8 h depending on the road and ford conditions (OunTravela 4–5 h; Kabar 5–6 h; kgnomad 5–8 h).
stay: Yurt camps at the head of the valley: Kel-Suu Yurt Camp (2GIS: from 1800 som, up to 40 beds, breakfast, cafe, horses; +996 552 979 696), Golden Moon (kgnomad), Jyrgal's Yurt Camp. 2024 prices (too.kg): a yurt for 2 — 1700 som/person with breakfast, for 4–7 — 1500 som/person, meals 800 som; 2026 (kgnomad): 1500–2500+ som/person with meals. Conditions are simple: mattresses on the floor, a stove, an outdoor toilet (NomadCar).
net: There is no mobile signal (NomadCar, kgnomad 2026; too.kg); some camps have Wi-Fi (2GIS — Kel-Suu Yurt Camp), the type and quality are not confirmed.
entry: No fee for entering the valley was found. A border permit is mandatory: CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn region, one week) / €50 urgent; tour.too.kg — 3000 som (2026).
transfer: Jeep Naryn — Kok-Kyya — Naryn: 13,000–20,000+ som per car, ≈3500–5000 som/person for four (kgnomad, 07.2026). Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn — 600 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026).
bring: Border permit and passport; warm clothes and a sleeping bag/thermal underwear (0…−5 °C at night), a rain jacket, sunscreen and sunglasses; shoes for fords; cash in som; a flashlight, power bank, offline maps; a trash bag.
warn: A border zone on the border with China — they won't let you through without a permit. The fords across the Kok-Kyya are dangerous in flood and in the second half of the day. Elevation ~3300 m, abrupt weather. No signal or medical aid — report your route in advance. Don't set off on your own routes in the valley without clearing it: exact directions are confirmed with the border guards (eurasia.travel).
food: In the yurt camps — home-style Kyrgyz cooking: beshbarmak, shorpo, boorsok, kaymak, dairy products from yaks and mares (editorial; meals ~800 som each — too.kg 2024).
reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.8/5, 9 reviews, No. 3 of 16 in Naryn (as of 07.10.2026). Google Maps “Kok-Kyya Canyon” — no rating (check 03.10.2026). Pros: wild nature, yaks, canyons, few people; cons: a very hard and expensive road, fords without bridges, a short season, the need for a permit; in 2026 — complaints about trash (time.kg).
p.sum: Kok-Kyya is the end of the road and the base for Lake Kel-Suu: yurt camps stand here (Kel-Suu Yurt Camp, Meder's camp, Jyrgal and others). You can get here only with a border permit and in a 4×4 with a driver: Naryn → At-Bashy → Kyndy → Ak-Sai, ≈145–160 km, 4.5–6 h (a round-trip jeep 13,000–20,000+ som per car). A night in a yurt 1500–2500 som with meals, in the morning to the lake on foot 7.5–9 km, on horseback ≈2000–2500 som or by UAZ 10,000 som/car. Fill up, withdraw cash and stock up in Naryn.

p.season: Late June — 25 September: the camps operate (best mid-July to August). June — snow and high fords; September — night frosts and few tourists. October to May: the road through Ak-Sai is under snow, the camps are closed (Meder's family has a herder's house/trailer in winter by arrangement, Nomad's Land).
p.budget.economy: ≈12,000–17,000 som/person for 3 days (group of 4): marshrutka 600×2, jeep 3500–5000, permit 3000, yurt 2 nights ≈3000–5000, horse 2000 or on foot.
p.permits: A border permit is mandatory (the border zone of At-Bashy district on the border with China). Ways to arrange it: 1) tour.too.kg — 3000 som (all border zones) / $35 for the Kel-Suu—Kok-Kyya—Chatyr-Kol zone; 5–7 working days; office at Isanov St. 105/3, Bishkek (2026). 2) CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn region only, ~1 week), €35 (several regions), €50 urgent in 2 working days (stage 1); Nomad's Land: from Naryn it's fastest — a few days, via Bishkek — up to 2 weeks. Step by step: (1) send a scan of your passport and the trip dates (WhatsApp/form); (2) pay a 50% prepayment; (3) the Border Service reviews it for ~1 week; (4) pick up the paper original in Bishkek or Naryn (or via a guide/tour — then send a copy of your passport a few days ahead). The permit is valid for up to 1 month. It is checked at military posts at Kyndy Pass/the entrance to the Ak-Sai valley (2 posts per Eurasia Travel) — you need the original permit with the stamp and your passport. Photographing the posts is forbidden. No fee for entering the lake/valley was found. JoN (04.2026) advises applying for the permit through CBT Naryn at least 2 weeks ahead; if traveling independently the driver needs a permit too.
p.access: With children — from school age (elevation ~3300 m, long jolting, fords); life at the camp is simple — mattresses on the floor, a stove, an outdoor toilet, no hot shower (JoN). Older people — only in good health. With a stroller — not accessible. With a dog — not advisable (herding dogs, border zone).
